title: Primary & Enteric Hyperoxaluria Masterclass
description: 整合 Primary Hyperoxaluria (PH1, PH2, PH3) 基因代謝障礙、Enteric Hyperoxaluria 腸道脂肪吸收不良與 Oxalate Nephropathy 之專科課程。

sections.title: Module 1: Metabolic Pathways of Primary Hyperoxaluria (PH1, PH2, PH3) & Pyridoxine Response
sections.content:
### 1. Metabolic Enzyme Defect Matrix

| Subtype | Mutated Gene | Defective Enzyme | Subcellular Location | Accumulating Toxic Metabolites | Pyridoxine (B6) Responsiveness |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 1 (PH1) | AGXT | Alanine-Glyoxylate Aminotransferase (AGT) | Peroxisome (Misfolding / Mitochondrial Peroxisomal Mistargeting in Gly170Arg) | Glyoxylate ➔ Oxalate & Glycolate | ~30% Responsive (especially Gly170Arg mutation) |
| Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 2 (PH2) | GRHPR | Glyoxylate Reductase / Hydroxypyruvate Reductase | Cytosol | Oxalate & L-Glyceric Acid | Non-responsive |
| Primary Hyperoxaluria Type 3 (PH3) | HOGA1 | 4-Hydroxy-2-Oxoglutarate Aldolase | Mitochondria | Oxalate & 4-Hydroxy-2-Oxoglutarate (HOG) | Non-responsive |

### 2. High-Yield Differential Comparison Table

| Feature | Primary Hyperoxaluria (PH1) | Enteric Hyperoxaluria | Dietary / Idiopathic Calcium Oxalate Stones |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Urinary Oxalate Excretion | Extremely High (> 1.0 mmol/day or > 90 mg/day) | High (0.5–1.0 mmol/day) | Mildly Elevated (0.45–0.6 mmol/day) |
| Systemic Oxalosis Risk | High (ESKD Leads to Deposition in Bone, Heart, Retina) | Rare (Unless Combined with Severe Dehydration) | Absent |
| Intestinal Calcium Availability | Normal | Reduced (Calcium Bound to Unabsorbed Fatty Acids) | Normal |
| Key Diagnostic Biomarker | Elevated Plasma / Urinary Glycolate & AGXT Gene Mutation | History of Malabsorption / Bariatric Surgery | Hypercalciuria, Low Citrate |

### 3. Pathophysiological Decision Tree

AGXT Gene Mutation (PH1) ➔ Loss of Peroxisomal AGT Activity ➔ Inability to Convert Glyoxylate to Glycine ➔ Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) Oxidizes Excess Glyoxylate to Oxalate ➔ Massive Urinary Calcium Oxalate Supersaturation ➔ Nephrocalcinosis, Recurrent Urolithiasis & Early ESKD ➔ Systemic Oxalosis (Deposition in Bone, Joints, Vasculature).

### 4. Conceptual Trap Analysis

**Trap**: 忽視特定 AGXT 基因突變 (如 Gly170Arg) 對 Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 的治療反應。
**Analysis**: Pyridoxine 是 AGT Cofactor。在帶有 Gly170Arg 或 Phe152Ile 突變的 PH1 患者中，高劑量 Pyridoxine (5–20 mg/kg/day) 可穩定 misfolded 酵素並將其導向 Peroxisome，使約 30% 患者的尿草酸排出量下降大於 30% 甚至完全正常化。因此確診 PH1 後應立即進行 Pyridoxine 刺激測試與基因檢測。

sections.title: Module 2: Enteric Hyperoxaluria Pathophysiology & Bariatric Surgery Risk
sections.content:
### 1. Intestinal Luminal Physiology Matrix

| Physiology State | Luminal Fatty Acids | Luminal Free Calcium | Soluble Oxalate Availability | Colonic Oxalate Permeability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Normal State | Low | Abundant | Low (Bound as Insoluble Calcium Oxalate) | Low |
| Malabsorption (Roux-en-Y / Malabsorptive Bowel) | Unabsorbed Free Fatty Acids High | Depleted (Calcium Saponified with Fatty Acids) | High (Unbound Free Oxalate Remains Soluble) | High (Bile Salts & Fatty Acids Increase Colonic Permeability) |

### 2. Pathophysiological Decision Tree

Fat Malabsorption (Crohn Disease, Pancreatic Insufficiency, Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass) ➔ Unabsorbed Fatty Acids Bind Luminal Calcium (Saponification) ➔ Depletion of Free Luminal Calcium ➔ Oxalate Cannot Form Insoluble Calcium Oxalate Precipitate ➔ Free Soluble Oxalate Increases in Colonic Lumen ➔ Bile Salts & Fatty Acids Increase Colonic Mucosal Permeability ➔ Massive Passive Colonic Absorption of Oxalate ➔ Enteric Hyperoxaluria & Acute Oxalate Nephropathy.

### 3. Conceptual Trap Analysis

**Trap**: 限制 Enteric Hyperoxaluria 患者的膳食 Calcium 攝取以防止 Calcium Oxalate 結石。
**Analysis**: 這是一個極為危險的迷思！在 Enteric Hyperoxaluria 中，限制飲食中的 Calcium 會進一步減少腸道內能與 Oxalate 結合的 Calcium，導致更多 Free Oxalate 在大腸被吸收，反而惡化 Hyperoxaluria。正確處置為口服 Calcium Carbonate / Calcium Citrate 隨餐給予，使其在腸道與 Oxalate 結合並隨糞便排出。

sections.title: Module 3: Oxalate Nephropathy Biopsy Histopathology & Systemic Oxalosis Management
sections.content:
### 1. Biopsy Histopathology & Polarized Light Matrix

| Histopathological Finding | Brightfield Light Microscopy | Polarized Light Microscopy | Von Kossa Staining |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Calcium Oxalate Crystals | Intratubular & Interstitial Abundant Crystals | Strongly Birefringent (Polychromatic / Fan-shaped / Radial Array) | Negative (Does not stain black like Calcium Phosphate) |
| Calcium Phosphate Crystals | Amorphous or Microcrystalline Deposits | Non-birefringent or Weakly Birefringent | Positive (Stains Dark Black) |

### 2. Pathophysiological Decision Tree

Renal Allograft Transplantation in Uncorrected PH1 ➔ High Systemic Oxalate Pool ➔ Rapid Deposition of Calcium Oxalate Crystals in Graft Tubules ➔ Early Allograft Failure ➔ Combined Liver-Kidney Transplantation (CLKT) or RNAi Therapy (Lumasiran) Needed to Suppress Hepatic Oxalate Production.

### 3. Conceptual Trap Analysis

**Trap**: Polarized Light 下看到晶體即認為是 Calcium Phosphate。
**Analysis**: Calcium Oxalate Strong Birefringence，呈現絢麗的多色或扇形放射狀形貌；而 Calcium Phosphate 晶體在偏振光下無birefringence性，且 Von Kossa 染色呈陽性黑色。臨床切片必須依此嚴格區分。

Polarized Microscopy Birefringence Features of Intratubular Calcium Oxalate Deposits.
